clue.text: Talking sweet talk in 20

indicators.note: talking means the words are to be heard spoken, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding such as mousse, and to talk idly is to jaw

explanation.surface: Someone is saying sweet nothings somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSSE (a sweet) plus JAW (talk) sounds like the Saskatchewan city of MOOSE JAW; 20 is CANADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Moose Jaw is a small city in Saskatchewan, so it is a place located in Canada.

clue.text: Flash major part (not small) outside gents

indicators.note: outside means the shortened word wraps around the other piece
not means the letter for small is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: the major part of something is most of it
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
gents are men

explanation.surface: A big chunk of something, minus the small bit, surrounds a gentlemen's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' is the instant, not a burst of light; 'not small' leaves MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is an instant, a very brief stretch of time, as in 'back in a flash'.

clue.text: Fancy 9 without borders out of control

indicators.note: out of control means the remaining letters run wild into a new order
without borders means the first and last letters of the city are removed

parts.note: the answer to 9 across is the Canadian city Montreal

explanation.surface: Something fancy in a Canadian city runs amok once its edges are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: MONTREAL without its first and last letters is ONTREA, which 'out of control' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborately decorated, a close synonym of ornate.

clue.text: Schemer in time makes mistakes

indicators.note: in means the schemer sits inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a treacherous, scheming person

explanation.definitionFit: Errata are a list of errors, especially those corrected in a printed book.

clue.text: Experts on bodies converting to Satanism

clue.text: Report publishes "bear in 20"

explanation.walkthrough: PRINTS spoken sounds like PRINCE; RUPERT Bear is a British children's cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Rupert is a port city in British Columbia, so it lies within Canada.

clue.text: Shortly, see person out, then return

indicators.note: out means the letters are to be put out of their order
shortly means the word see loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Briefly show a visitor the door, then come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims SEE to SE; SE plus PERSON is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a return in the sense of a reply or answer to something.

clue.text: Pole and its location, around circle, numbing

parts.note: the North Pole lies in the Arctic

clue.text: Never swelling up about head of Mafia in 20

clue.text: Daytime unaffected in 20

explanation.definitionFit: Montreal is the largest city in Quebec, a Canadian province.

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of religious

clue.text: Signs books in 20, perhaps

clue.text: Wrap fashion designer has on

parts.note: Coco Chanel was a famous French fashion designer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couturier is wearing a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is a protective silky wrapping, and figuratively any enveloping cover.

clue.text: Where some mites taking refuge set up business

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place or refuge

explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses LAIR to RIAL; dust mites are tiny creatures living in house dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Business used as a modifier, as in business estate, means relating to trade and manufacturing, like industrial.

clue.text: Barely audible pop, when starved of oxygen?

definitions.text: Barely audible pop, when starved of oxygen?

parts.words: Barely audible pop, when starved of oxygen?
parts.note: sound needs air to travel, so a pop in a near-vacuum would be scarcely heard: a musical direction for very quiet playing

explanation.surface: A bang barely heard in thin air.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical term means very softly, so a sound marked this way is barely audible.

clue.text: Spooner's game over in practice

explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a rehearsal or trial, a practice attempt before the real thing.

clue.text: Privileged, one given capital to invest in transport at all stations

explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the national capital, a city in Canada.

clue.text: Sailor holding bend in rope, figures stable
